🚨 BIG: India's #Sarvam AI Unveils Ambitious 1 Trillion+ Parameter Foundation Model & Claims AI Pricing 5.5× Lower Than Global Rivals 🇮🇳🧠

Sarvam AI has announced plans to develop India's first 1 #trillion-plus parameter frontier foundation model, built entirely from scratch in India. The announcement marks one of the country's most ambitious AI initiatives and aligns with the Government of India's vision of building sovereign AI capabilities under the IndiaAI Mission.

🔹 Key Highlights:

✅ 1 Trillion+ Parameters: Sarvam's next-generation model aims to operate at frontier scale, placing India among the select nations attempting to build trillion-parameter AI systems.

✅ Built from Scratch: Unlike many AI models that are fine-tuned from existing open-source LLMs, Sarvam's model will be trained natively using its own architecture, training pipeline and datasets.

✅ 5.5× Lower AI Pricing: Sarvam says its inference pricing is up to 5.5 times cheaper than comparable global AI offerings, making advanced AI significantly more affordable for Indian developers, startups, enterprises and government agencies. The company says its Sarvam 105B model is priced at roughly $0.80 per million blended tokens, compared with around $4.50 for GPT-5.4 Mini and $9 for Gemini 3.5 Flash.

✅ Multimodal AI: The upcoming model will support text, speech, vision and advanced reasoning, enabling next-generation AI assistants and enterprise applications.

🔹 New AI Products Announced

• Sarvam Vision 2.0 – Advanced multimodal vision model for document understanding and image intelligence.
• Sarvam Vision Edge – Enterprise-grade document AI platform for OCR, invoices, forms, PDFs and workflow automation.
• Bulbul V4 – Enhanced multilingual text-to-speech model with more natural, human-like voices.
• Upgraded speech recognition, conversational AI and AI agent capabilities for enterprise deployment.

🔹 Potential Applications

• Government digital services
• Citizen AI assistants
• Education & personalized tutoring
• Healthcare decision support
• Agriculture advisory
• Banking & financial services
• Legal and judicial research
• Manufacturing & enterprise automation
• Scientific research and software development

Building a trillion-parameter foundation model will require massive AI infrastructure, including thousands of high-performance GPUs, high-speed networking, enormous multilingual datasets and advanced distributed training systems. While parameter count alone does not determine AI capability, successfully delivering such a model would represent a major technological milestone for India's #AI ecosystem.

If successful, #Sarvam AI could position India among the world's leading AI nations by developing indigenous frontier-scale AI models that reduce dependence on foreign platforms while accelerating innovation across government, industry and research.

whoever leaked this has bigger balls than sense

two researchers replaced $7,500 of human grading with $77.81 of model calls, and the number that fell out should stop anyone shipping an agent this week: the judge disagrees with itself 13.6% of the time

it also prefers whichever answer it saw first, 72% of the time. cross-judge agreement is a kappa of 0.51: the statistical polite word for guessing

this is Eval Engineering, the layer that arrives after loops and graphs, and it installs into the agent you already pay for:

- run every comparison both ways and average the two, because one production judge picked whichever answer sat in the first slot 72% of the time
- stop shipping on a single verdict: recovering the reference answer took 11 repeated trials before a majority vote landed it, and 15 on the questions that actually mattered
- report the chance-corrected agreement instead of raw match, since the gap between those two ran 33 to 41 points on the same benchmark
- never let a model grade its own family, because self-preference tracks capability upward rather than falling away as models improve
- test stability and bias together, since two judges already running in production held above 0.95 on repeat while carrying severe positional preference
- freeze the rubric wording and version it, because semantically identical templates flipped the majority outcome in a quarter of tested cases
- write the rubric as one observable pass condition rather than a bundle of scores, so a coin-flip preference cannot hide inside an average
- let plain code take every objective call, did the test pass, does the file exist, did the state change, and leave the judge only what genuinely needs reading
- make the verdict do something structural to the run in flight, reject the handoff, swap the node, quarantine the branch, or you have built a dashboard

the catch is that your judge is a measurement instrument nobody calibrates: single-trial judging is too noisy for anything you would stake money on, and the same judges reordered by as much as 14 positions depending on which benchmark you asked

so the loop has to converge on the spec rather than on the score, because optimise against a judge long enough and the agent learns to look right instead of being right

Apparently someone impersonating as Papergames official and sent a complaint towards a user on Douyin for creating content about Valko. And about an hour later or so the complaint was withdrawn. Complaint statement translation on last paragraph 👇🏻

With a little bit of research I did, apparently they do not require business information to file a complaint on behalf of a company BUT it does require real name verification, ID etc.

So I'm assuming, the person behind the complaint chickened out. People are also mentioning that the statement isn't consistent with how Papergames would write on their complaints, which is more formal & inclusive of legal terms.
